correctness.rationale: The sampling is independent endpoints, not an invariant random line. Same-edge endpoints cause zero-area atom sum length_i^2/P^2. At vertex i, a corner triangle has area (sin(alpha_i)/2)*xy, with ordered incident side-pair domain area t(1+log(a_i*b_i/t)); two endpoint orders yield the displayed 4s/P^2 csc angle terms. For nonincident side pairs, the only zero-area limiting chords approach an intervening edge and require both endpoint offsets O(s), hence O_K(s^2) after bounded local linear geometry; in triangles an additional near-whole-corner complement event is also O(s^2). Conditional -log normalized endpoint distances are independent exponentials; their sum has gamma(2,1) density, share exactly uniform, and normalized area has density (T-log z)/(T+1) with TV distance 1/(e(T+1)) from uniform. The global csc second-derivative >=1 yields coefficient 2 in angular variance with equality equiangular and rhombi witnessing sharpness; the independent uniform-product CDF establishes the triangle expression for every 0<s<A/2. A separate exact evaluation of the triangle formula at z=.01 was 0.056101869364914..., consistent with the proof. The remainder is for fixed nondegenerate K, not uniform in degenerations.

value.rationale: A complete two-endpoint cutting law for arbitrary convex polygons with nonzero-area conditioning, explicit joint rare-event marks, angle-only leading invariant, sharp rigidity and exact triangle benchmark is a natural geometric-probability result. Prior random-line and one-point+direction protocols have different small-area exponents; multiple-point hull missing-area observables do not answer the two-point cut problem. The invariant, conditional marked limit and sharp stability supply specific reusable facts.

final_claim: For two independent uniform-by-arclength endpoints of a fixed genuine convex polygon boundary, nonzero small cut-off areas obey the two-term s log(1/s) and s expansion with coefficient 4 sum csc(interior angle)/P^2, a zero-atom formula, sharp angular-rigidity inequality, joint corner/log-split/area/orientation total-variation limit, and exact triangle law.
